title: Why Evidence-Based Practice? Three Legs of the Stool

hook.en: "We have always done it this way" has hurt patients before. But "the study says so" can hurt too, if it ignores the person in front of you. Evidence-based practice is not a cookbook. It is a three-legged stool, and a stool with one leg falls over.
hook.ur: "Hum hamesha aise hi karte aaye hain" ne pehle bhi mareezon ko nuqsan pohanchaya hai. Lekin "study kehti hai" bhi nuqsan de sakta hai, agar saamne baithe insaan ko nazar-andaaz kare. Evidence-based practice recipe book nahi. Yeh teen taangon wali kursi hai, aur ek taang wali kursi gir jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name the three legs of evidence-based practice, explain what happens when one leg is missing, and show how to bring research, experience and patient values into one decision.
goal.ur: End tak aap evidence-based practice ki teen taangein batayenge, samjhayenge ke ek taang na ho to kya hota hai, aur research, tajurba aur mareez ki values ko ek faisle mein jorna dikhayenge.

text.en: **Evidence-based practice (EBP)** means using the best available research, combined with your clinical expertise and the patient's values and circumstances, to decide care. Research alone cannot decide, because studies describe averages and your patient is one person. Experience alone cannot decide, because we remember our successes and forget patients who quietly dropped out. Values alone cannot decide, because patients cannot choose among options they do not know.
text.ur: **Evidence-based practice (EBP)** ka matlab hai behtareen dastiyab research ko apne clinical tajurbe aur mareez ki values aur halaat ke saath mila kar care ka faisla karna. Akeli research faisla nahi kar sakti, kyunke studies average batati hain aur aap ka mareez ek insaan hai. Akela tajurba faisla nahi kar sakta, kyunke hum apni kamyabiyan yaad rakhte hain aur khamoshi se chhor jane wale mareez bhool jate hain. Akeli values bhi faisla nahi kar sakti, kyunke mareez un options mein se chun nahi sakte jo unhein maloom nahi.

text.en: Think of a **three-legged stool**. Research is one leg, your clinical experience the second and the patient's values the third. Cut any leg short and you sit crooked. A therapist who only follows studies becomes a robot, only follows habit becomes a dinosaur and only follows the patient's wishes becomes a vending machine.
text.ur: **Teen taangon wali kursi** sochein. Research ek taang, aap ka clinical tajurba doosri aur mareez ki values teesri. Koi taang chhoti kar dein to aap tirchay baithte hain. Jo therapist sirf studies par chale woh robot, sirf aadat par chale woh dinosaur aur sirf mareez ki khwahish par chale woh vending machine ban jata hai.

title.en: What happens when one leg of the stool is missing
title.ur: Jab kursi ki ek taang na ho to kya hota hai

headers.en: What it looks like in clinic

rows.en: "I do what I was taught years ago, and it works for me"
rows.ur: "Jo saalon pehle sikha wohi karta hoon, mere liye kaam karta hai"

rows.en: Ineffective or even harmful treatments continue for decades
rows.ur: Be-asar ya nuqsandeh ilaaj dehaiyon chalte rehte hain

rows.en: Applying a trial result to every patient without adjusting for who they are
rows.ur: Har mareez par trial ka nateeja bina uski shakhsiyat dekhe lagana

rows.en: Unsafe or unfit plans for complex, older or frail patients
rows.ur: Pechida, buzurg ya kamzor mareezon ke liye ghair mehfooz ya na-munasib plans

rows.en: Prescribing a daily programme the patient cannot do at work or home
rows.ur: Aisi rozana programme dena jo mareez kaam ya ghar par nahi kar sakta

rows.en: The patient stops coming back, and the plan fails quietly
rows.ur: Mareez aana chhor deta hai, aur plan khamoshi se nakam ho jata hai

title.ur: EBP ka paanch qadam ka chakkar

steps.title: Ask
steps.detail: Turn the patient's problem into a clear, answerable clinical question. || Poochhein

steps.title: Acquire
steps.detail: Search for the best evidence, starting with guidelines and systematic reviews. || Hasil karein

steps.title: Appraise
steps.detail: Judge whether the study is believable, what it found and whether it applies. || Parkhein

steps.title: Apply
steps.detail: Combine the result with your experience and what this patient wants, and decide together. || Lagu karein

steps.title: Assess
steps.detail: Check whether it worked for this patient, and change the plan if not. || Jaanchein

question.en: A trial shows a treatment helps on average, but your 80-year-old patient lives alone and cannot attend daily. What does EBP say?
question.ur: Ek trial batata hai ke ilaaj average mein madad karta hai, lekin aap ki 80 saal ki mareeza akeli rehti hai aur roz nahi aa sakti. EBP kya kehta hai?

text.en: Follow the trial exactly, because research always wins
text.ur: Trial ko hubahu follow karein, kyunke research hamesha jeet-ti hai

feedback.en: EBP does not ignore the patient's circumstances.
feedback.ur: EBP mareez ke halaat ko nazar-andaaz nahi karta.

text.en: Ignore the trial and use whatever you always use
text.ur: Trial ko nazar-andaaz karein aur wohi karein jo hamesha karte hain

feedback.en: That is the missing research leg.
feedback.ur: Yeh research ki ghayab taang hai.

text.en: Adapt the plan using the evidence, your experience and her circumstances, and agree it with her
text.ur: Evidence, apne tajurbe aur uske halaat se plan dhalein aur uske saath tay karein

feedback.en: Yes — the evidence informs the decision but does not replace judgement or the patient's situation.
feedback.ur: Haan — evidence faisle ko rehnumai deta hai lekin judgement ya mareez ke halaat ki jagah nahi leta.

question.en: A senior therapist says, "In 20 years, everyone I treated with this technique got better." Which leg of EBP is being relied on alone, and what is the main weakness?
question.ur: Ek senior therapist kehta hai, "20 saal mein jis ko is technique se ilaaj diya sab theek ho gaye." EBP ki kaun si taang akeli istemal ho rahi hai, aur sab se badi kamzori kya hai?

text.en: Research alone; the therapist is quoting a published study
text.ur: Sirf research; therapist shaya shuda study quote kar raha hai

feedback.en: He is quoting memory, not a study.
feedback.ur: Woh yaadasht quote kar raha hai, study nahi.

text.en: Experience alone; people who did not improve or never returned are forgotten, and many would have improved anyway
text.ur: Sirf tajurba; jo theek na hue ya wapas na aaye woh bhool jate hain, aur bohat se khud hi theek ho jate

feedback.en: Yes — selective memory and natural recovery make experience alone misleading.
feedback.ur: Haan — chunindah yaadasht aur qudrati recovery tajurbe ko akele gumrah kar deti hain.

text.en: Patient values alone; patients liked the technique
text.ur: Sirf mareez ki values; mareezon ko technique pasand aayi

feedback.en: Liking a treatment does not prove it works.
feedback.ur: Ilaaj pasand aana sabit nahi karta ke kaam karta hai.

question.en: Which of these is part of the EBP cycle?
question.ur: In mein se EBP ke chakkar ka hissa kaun sa hai?

text.en: Buying the newest device so patients think you are modern
text.ur: Naya aala khareedna taake mareez aap ko modern samjhein

text.en: Turning the patient's problem into an answerable question, then searching for evidence
text.ur: Mareez ke masle ko jawab dene ke qabil sawal banana, phir evidence dhoondna

feedback.en: Yes — asking a good question is step one.
feedback.ur: Haan — achha sawal poochhna pehla qadam hai.

text.en: Quoting a famous professor in every session
text.ur: Har session mein mashhoor professor ka hawala dena

feedback.en: Authority is not the same as evidence.
feedback.ur: Ikhtiyar aur evidence ek cheez nahi.

text.en: **Thinking EBP means "only randomised trials" or "ignore your judgement".** It means using the best available evidence, which can be a guideline, a review, a cohort study or a patient preference when no trial exists, and letting judgement and values shape how it is used. "No evidence" often means "not studied yet", not "does not work".
text.ur: **Yeh samajhna ke EBP ka matlab "sirf randomised trials" ya "apna judgement nazar-andaaz karo" hai.** Matlab hai dastiyab behtareen evidence istemal karna, jo guideline, review, cohort study ya jab trial na ho to mareez ki pasand bhi ho sakti hai, aur judgement aur values ko is ke istemal ka rukh tay karne dena. "Evidence nahi" ka matlab aksar "abhi study nahi hui" hota hai, "kaam nahi karta" nahi.

text.en: **Say it to the patient.** For example: "Here is what research tells us about your problem. Here is what I have seen work in people like you. Now tell me what matters most to you, so we can choose together." This turns evidence into a conversation, and patients who help choose tend to stick to the plan.
text.ur: **Mareez ko kahein.** Misaal: "Yeh hai jo research aap ke masle ke baare mein batati hai. Yeh hai jo main ne aap jaise logon mein kaam karte dekha hai. Ab aap batayein aap ke liye sab se zyada kya ahem hai, taake hum milkar chunein." Isse evidence baat cheet ban jata hai, aur jo mareez chunne mein shamil hon woh plan par qayam rehte hain.

question.en: Is "it worked for my last ten patients" good evidence?
question.ur: Kya "mere pichhle das mareezon par kaam kiya" achha saboot hai?

answer.en: It is weak evidence. Without a comparison group, you cannot tell treatment effect from natural recovery, regression to the mean or the patient's expectation. Your ten patients are valuable as clinical experience and as a reason to ask a question, but not as proof. The next lesson shows why.
answer.ur: Yeh kamzor saboot hai. Comparison group ke baghair aap ilaaj ke asar ko qudrati recovery, regression to the mean ya mareez ki umeed se alag nahi kar sakte. Aap ke das mareez clinical tajurbe ke taur par aur sawal poochhne ki wajah ke taur par qeemti hain, lekin saboot ke taur par nahi. Agla lesson batayega kyun.

beats.patient: A 45-year-old teacher has chronic neck pain. A guideline recommends exercise and education over passive treatments. She says she cannot afford many visits and wants quick relief.
beats.assessment: The guideline supports exercise, her wish for quick relief is a real value, and her limited visits are a circumstance.
beats.treatment: You teach a short home exercise programme with a plan for a couple of visits, explain that passive relief may help a little for a short time, and agree on how you will both check progress in two weeks.
beats.reassess: She follows the plan because it fits her life, and you review and adapt it at the next visit.

text.en: **Evidence does not override safety.** If a patient has red flags, such as unexplained weight loss, night pain or neurological loss, you refer first, whatever a guideline says about treatment. Be careful with evidence from patients unlike yours, such as young athletes' trials applied to frail elders.
text.ur: **Evidence safety ko override nahi karta.** Agar mareez mein red flags hon, jaise be-wajah wazan kam hona, raat ka dard ya neurological nuqsan, to guideline kuch bhi kahe pehle refer karein. Un mareezon ke evidence se ehtiyat karein jo aap ke mareezon se mukhtalif hon, jaise young athletes ke trials kamzor buzurgon par lagana.

text.en: Sackett and colleagues defined evidence-based medicine as the conscientious, explicit and judicious use of current best evidence in making decisions about individual patients, and stressed that it integrates individual clinical expertise with the best external evidence. Haynes, Devereaux and Guyatt later made patient preferences and actions an explicit part of the model, alongside research evidence, clinical state and circumstances, and clinical expertise.
text.ur: Sackett aur saathiyon ne evidence-based medicine ko mareezon ke faislon mein maujooda behtareen evidence ka imaandar, saaf aur samajhdaar istemal qarar diya, aur zor diya ke yeh infiradi clinical maharat ko bairooni behtareen evidence ke saath jorta hai. Haynes, Devereaux aur Guyatt ne baad mein mareez ki pasand aur amal ko research evidence, clinical halat aur halaat, aur clinical maharat ke saath model ka saaf hissa banaya.

text.en: **Research, Me, You.** Research evidence, my experience, and your (the patient's) values: three legs, one decision.
text.ur: **Research, Main, Aap.** Research evidence, mera tajurba, aur aap (mareez) ki values: teen taangein, ek faisla.

summary.en: EBP combines best research, clinical experience and patient values; no leg works alone.
summary.ur: EBP behtareen research, clinical tajurba aur mareez ki values ko jorta hai; koi taang akeli kaam nahi karti.

summary.en: Use the five steps: ask, acquire, appraise, apply, assess.
summary.ur: Paanch qadam istemal karein: poochhein, hasil karein, parkhein, lagu karein, jaanchein.

summary.en: "No evidence" often means not studied yet, and evidence never overrides safety.
summary.ur: "Evidence nahi" ka matlab aksar abhi study nahi hui, aur evidence safety ko kabhi override nahi karta.

back.ur: Poochhein, hasil karein, parkhein, lagu karein, jaanchein.

front.en: Why is "it worked for my patients" weak evidence?
front.ur: "Mere mareezon par kaam kiya" kamzor saboot kyun hai?

back.en: No comparison group, selective memory and natural recovery.
back.ur: Comparison group nahi, chunindah yaadasht aur qudrati recovery.

front.en: Does "no evidence" mean a treatment does not work?
front.ur: Kya "evidence nahi" ka matlab ilaaj kaam nahi karta?

back.en: No; it often means it has not been studied well yet.
back.ur: Nahi; aksar matlab hota hai ke abhi achhi tarah study nahi hua.

note.ur: Soch ke shortcuts hamein kaise gumrah karte hain.
